name: QA crew
description: Turns a ticket into test cases and automated tests, runs them, then drafts the sign-off or the bug.

briefing.jql: project = {{project}} AND {{scope}} AND statusCategory = "In Progress" AND issuetype not in subTaskIssueTypes() ORDER BY priority DESC
briefing.rankPrompt: You plan a QA engineer's day. Put first the tickets that are waiting for testing or review, then the ones still in development that will arrive soon, by priority. Mark as not actionable the tickets that are operational, legal, commercial or follow-up work with nothing to test.

branches.label: Pick regression suites
Turn the ticket into test cases
branches.message: Turning the acceptance criteria into test cases

workflow.label: Write the automated tests
workflow.prompt:
Write automated tests for this ticket in this repository, following its conventions exactly.

Rules:
- First read the project's contributor notes (README, CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING), the test configuration, and two or three existing tests close to this feature. Use the same framework, helpers and naming.
- Put everything in ONE test file whose name includes the ticket key in lowercase without the dash. If a test file for this ticket already exists, extend that file instead of creating another.
- Never modify any other existing file. If you need a new helper, create a NEW file.
- Never read or write .env files and never hardcode credentials.
- One test per case below, with the case title as the test title. If a case cannot be automated with what the repository offers, keep it as a skipped or pending test with a comment that says what is missing.
- Do not run anything. You only have file tools.

Return testFile as the path relative to the repository root, otherFiles as any other file you created, and a two-sentence summary that says how many cases are automated and how many are pending.

Test cases:
{{cases.cases|numbered}}

Ticket {{ticket.key}}: {{ticket.summary}}

{{ticket.description}}

Add negative and edge cases
Draft the bug report
